status: Recorded native outcomes resume at startup and on controls; both-mode SIGKILL, original-context restoration and lost HTTP settlement ACK checks pass. Complete command recovery remains in progress.

shared_implementation.facade: Host.recover_pending is shared by controls and the startup inventory; Journal.reconcile_original reuses complete, publish and settle.
shared_implementation.ownership: Normal command producers and recovery share bounded per-host original-authority claims. The claim lives through registered publication/settlement tasks and drops with the last owner.
shared_implementation.native_inventory: Read bounded original command records with invocation, durable outcome and positive cleanup state; select requested records before copying their payloads. Preserve the anchored namespace across retries.
shared_implementation.adapters: OriginalCommandJournal supplies pinned HTTP primitives for the same service/paired outcome policy. No provider selection, source reload, LSP restart or command dispatch occurs.
shared_implementation.startup: run_server_until registers a private inventory worker before accepting requests. It retries unavailable original state, resumes only recorded outcomes and honors coordinator shutdown.

behavior: Return an already-recorded native result even when the original folder or callback is temporarily unavailable; do not use that result as permission to mutate a replacement folder.
Reopen and acquire the original full physical folder gate, reread its native record, verify the enduring issuer, and publish only the original result/cleanup receipt.
Retry initial callback/folder failures in an owned task without a browser wakeup. Keep the original claim through later manual acknowledgement and exact backend/native settlement.
After an accepted backend settlement reply is lost, preserve the native owner. Join the exact terminal worker/outcome receipt and retire the native record only after an acknowledged repeat.
Known outcomes with no positive cleanup proof remain pending; missing legacy credentials/origins do not become new execution or cleanup authority.

verification.qualification: The production implementation passed the complete native suite before only one test-support example and two integration-fixture files changed. Final all-target/default/Windows profiles and all HTTP cases reran on those stronger process tests. Earlier shared checks retain identical package/build inputs and immutable executable provenance.

process_contract: The disposable example uses the existing test-support private-home constructor and otherwise runs the production native HTTP host and managed-command helper. The normal bridge gains no private-home CLI or environment override.

A real child process receives Stop, persists and returns the no-dispatch result, then is killed with SIGKILL and reaped. A distinct successor process reads the same original namespace and completes recovery after acknowledgement.

Each mode checks normal startup, callback outage, original-root substitution/restoration and an actual connection failure after the real Store commits settlement. The latter blocks further callbacks while the test proves backend idle does not release the native folder.

No command control or language request wakes final recovery. An ordinary native writer eventually succeeds; the original root/source and replacement sentinel survive, and the LSP execution marker is absent.
limits: The process-crash matrix covers positive no-dispatch rejections. Completed/uncertain dispatched-command crash cases and original watcher completion receipts still need verification and implementation.

Concurrent peer-producer retirement and failures that begin after an existing publisher enters its settlement wait loop still need work. Original record disappearance must stop a stale local publisher without granting mutation authority.
History-pruned final-ACK recovery, early Cancel retirement without an invented public outcome, and callback rebinding with original-scope proof remain unfinished.

The backend in this HTTP fixture uses real Store CAS and a private original issuer, not a fresh deployed Spin/browser run. All original writer/platform/cache/resource/full-CI/application requirements remain active.
